### `env-file-inventory`

Report which repositories track a real environment file and which only ship an example

- **Script** — `scripts/learned/env-file-inventory.js`
- **Run** — `node .claude/skills/gh-commands/scripts/learned/env-file-inventory.js --json`
- **Recognised phrasings** — "which repos have env files committed", "do any of my repos track a .env", "environment variable file inventory", "find committed dotenv files", "which projects contain environment variables"
- **Parameters** — `--owner` — GitHub login; defaults to config.json defaultOwner; `--cache` — clone cache directory; `--include-forks` — include forks, which are excluded by default; `--json` — machine-readable output
- **gh calls** — `gh repo list <owner> --limit 500 --json name,isFork,visibility,defaultBranchRef`
- **Notes** — Separates a tracked .env from a .env.example plus a gitignore rule, which is the same convention working correctly. Shallow clones, because code search misses dotfiles and throttles.

### `repos-by-name-pattern`

List the repositories of an owner whose name matches a pattern

- **Script** — `scripts/learned/repos-by-name-pattern.js`
- **Run** — `node .claude/skills/gh-commands/scripts/learned/repos-by-name-pattern.js --pattern playwright`
- **Recognised phrasings** — "give me repos containing playwright in name", "which repositories have X in the name", "find my repos named something", "list repos matching a pattern", "repos whose name contains"
- **Parameters** — `--pattern` (required) — case-insensitive regex matched against the repository name; `--owner` — GitHub login; defaults to config.json defaultOwner; `--include-forks` — include forks, which are excluded by default; `--json` — machine-readable output
- **gh calls** — `gh repo list <owner> --limit <n> --json name,description,visibility,isFork,isArchived,pushedAt,primaryLanguage,stargazerCount,url`
- **Notes** — gh search repos matches description and README too, so it answers a different question; this filters on the name itself.

### `secret-scan`

Sweep every repository of an owner for credentials that look real

- **Script** — `scripts/learned/secret-scan.js`
- **Run** — `node .claude/skills/gh-commands/scripts/learned/secret-scan.js --json`
- **Recognised phrasings** — "do any of my repos contain secrets", "scan my github for leaked keys", "find hardcoded api keys and tokens", "check repositories for credentials", "secret leak audit across my projects"
- **Parameters** — `--owner` — GitHub login; defaults to config.json defaultOwner; `--cache` — clone cache directory; `--contextual` — also report low-confidence keyword hits, which are usually test data; `--json` — machine-readable output
- **gh calls** — `gh repo list <owner> --limit 500 --json name,isFork,visibility,defaultBranchRef`
- **Notes** — Vendor-prefixed tokens are reported as high confidence; keyword-plus-literal hits are suppressed unless asked for. Files whose job is to detect secrets are suppressed separately. Working tree only at clone depth 1 - git history is not scanned.
